lesson.subject: literacy
lesson.title: Feeling Clues
lesson.subtitle: Finding how a character feels from the words

studentTools: Printed Feeling Clues Finder, one per child
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
Point to A, B or C
boardSetup: A two-column chart on the board: Clue | Feeling
Room to write the sentence stem: I think ... feels ... because ...

resources.label: Feeling Clues Finder
resources.description: You Do. A short story with space to underline two clues, a clue chart, and the sentence stem.
resources.title: Feeling Clues Finder
resources.subtitle: Read. Find the clues. Name the feeling.

blocks.text: Zara waited at the school gate. Everyone else had gone home. She kicked a stone, then looked up the empty road again. Her lip began to wobble. Then a car turned the corner and Zara jumped up and waved with both arms.

steps: Underline two clues that show how Zara feels.
Write the feeling and the clue in the chart.

blocks.tip: Stretch: Zara has two feelings in this story. Find the clue for each one.

slides.notes: Open the lesson. One line: today we become feeling detectives and find the clues authors leave in the words.

Prep slide. Print the Feeling Clues Finder, one per child. Whiteboards ready for the checks. Draw the Clue | Feeling chart on the board before the lesson. The stories are original, written for this lesson, so nothing is assumed from earlier reading.

slides.title: How do you know how someone feels?
slides.prompt: Turn and tell: how can you tell without being told?

notes.answer: open - faces, bodies, what people do and say
beats: POINT to the four faces.
SAY: Here are four faces. Most of us can read a face in a second.
ASK: How can you tell how someone feels without being told?
20 sec. Turn and tell, partner A first.
EXPECT: their face, what they do, their voice
SCAN the room. Listen for actions.
80%+ -> next slide.
Less -> act a worried face, ask what gave it away, re-ask.
SAY: Authors do the same with words. Today we find the clues in the words.
trap: saying only the feeling word, not how they know.
Fix: ask what the body did, child names one clue.
notes.prep: Launch bridges reading faces, which every child can do, into reading words. Low-coupling, under 4 minutes.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to find clues in the words that show how a character feels.
successCriteria: I can find a clue in the words that shows the feeling.
I can say: I think ... feels ... because ...

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: Today we find clues in the words that show how a character feels.
SAY: Read the I can lines with me. Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: We'll start with the first one and build up together.
Finding the clue is our big goal today.
notes.prep: SC1 naming a feeling is reachable for all; SC2 finding the clue is the core target and the exit evidence; SC3 the full sentence stem is the stretch.

slides.meaning: A small hint that helps you work something out.
slides.example: Her hands shook. That is a clue she was scared.

notes.answer: a small hint that helps you work something out
beats: POINT to the word. SAY: Clue. Say it with me. Clue.
SAY: A clue is a small hint that helps you work something out.
Detectives use clues. Readers use clues too.
ASK: Her hands shook. What is the clue telling us?
10 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
EXPECT: she was scared, or nervous
trap: thinking a clue must be the feeling word itself.
Fix: cover the word scared, ask what the hands did, child says the clue.
notes.prep: The one word the lesson turns on. Rehearsed once here with a body clue, then used on every slide.

slides.title: Watch me find the clues
slides.extract: Mia stood at the edge of the pool. Her knees wobbled and she held the rail with both hands. She looked down at the water and took a big breath.
highlights: held the rail with both hands

notes.answer: worried - knees wobbled, held the rail, big breath
beats: READ it aloud once.
SAY: Now I'm going to hunt for clues about how Mia feels.
POINT to knees wobbled.
SAY: When my knees wobble, I feel worried. That's a clue.
POINT to held the rail with both hands.
SAY: She's holding on tight with both hands. That's another clue.
POINT to took a big breath.
SAY: So I think Mia feels worried, because her knees wobbled.
trap: Fix: ask what Mia's body did, child points to a body clue.
notes.stretch: Scared or excited? Find the clue that decides it.
notes.help: Cover all but the three highlighted phrases. Read only those.
notes.prep: The model: read, find a body clue, say the feeling with because. The sentence stem is said aloud here for the first time.

slides.title: Which words are the clue?
slides.prompt: Leo held his new kite. He grinned and ran across the park.

options.misconception: picks the thing, not what Leo's body did
picks the place, not a clue about the feeling

notes.answer: B - he grinned. Leo feels happy
beats: SAY: Here's a new story about Leo.
Listen for what his body does while I read it.
ASK: Which words are the clue about how Leo feels?
10 sec. Cue: voices off, everyone points to A, B or C.
EXPECT: pointing to B
SCAN the carpet, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call one child: so how does Leo feel?
Less -> grin, ask what that shows, re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: He grinned. That's what his body did, so it's our clue. Leo feels happy.
trap: Fix: ask what Leo's face did, child re-points to the grin.
notes.prep: First decision point, on a new text so it checks the move, not memory of the model. Under 80% means the We Do starts with acting the clues out.

slides.title: Find the clue together
slides.extract: Sam opened the box. He jumped up and clapped his hands. A puppy! he shouted, and he ran to hug his mum.

beats: CHORAL READ, everyone, together, on three.
SAY: Now it's your turn. Find one clue about how Sam feels.
ASK: Which words are a clue?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: jumped up, clapped, shouted, ran. Any one.
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call: which feeling?
Less -> jump and clap, ask how that feels, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Here are the three clues. Tick yours if it matches.
trap: Fix: ask what Sam's body did, child rewrites.
notes.stretch: Find a clue in what Sam said.
notes.help: Give jumped up, ask for one more.
notes.prep: Guided practice on a new text with the same move: body clue first, then the feeling with because. SC2.

slides.title: Which feeling? Find the clue.
slides.extract: Ali looked into his empty lunchbox. His shoulders dropped and a tear rolled down his cheek.

answers: sad - a tear rolled down his cheek

notes.answer: sad - shoulders dropped, a tear rolled down his cheek
beats: SAY: This one is just for you, so read it twice in your head.
ASK: How does Ali feel, and which words told you?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: sad, because a tear rolled down. ACCEPT: upset.
SCAN every board.
80%+ -> reveal, then the worksheet.
Less -> drop your shoulders, ask what that shows, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Sad. His shoulders dropped and a tear rolled down his cheek.
Tick or fix your feeling and your clue.
trap: Fix: ask what Ali's body did, child rewrites with a body clue.
notes.prep: The hinge before independence. A child with no clue on the board works with the teacher on the first clue of the worksheet story.

slides.title: Find the clues on your own
slides.task: Read the story on your sheet. Underline two clues. Write the feeling.

notes.answer: Zara: worried, then excited (lip wobbled; jumped up and waved)
beats: POINT to the task.
SAY: A new story about Zara. Read it twice, underline two clues, write the feeling.
SAY: Read, underline, write. Say the steps with me.
CIRCULATE. Listen for children reading the clue aloud before they write.
TIME 10 minutes. Early finishers find the second feeling in the story.
trap: Fix: ask which words show a body or voice, child underlines only those.
notes.stretch: Zara has two feelings. Find the clue for each.
notes.help: Read the story aloud. Point to lip began to wobble. Ask what it shows.
notes.prep: Independent application on a new text with the same stem. The sheet is the collected evidence for SC2 and SC3.

slides.title: Show what you know

visual.text: Ruby looked at the dark hall. She hugged her teddy tight.

questions: Write the feeling and one clue.

notes.answer: scared or worried - she hugged her teddy tight
beats: SAY: Here's a new story about Ruby. Read it twice in your head.
ASK: How does Ruby feel, and which words told you?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: scared, because she hugged her teddy tight. ACCEPT: worried.
RECORD who writes no clue, or the dark hall. Tomorrow's small group.
trap: writing the dark hall as the clue.
Fix: none now, record the name.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2 on a text no one has seen, one board per child. With the sheet, it drives tomorrow's grouping.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Tell your partner one clue word from today and the feeling it showed.
slides.notes: Read the three I can lines together. Thumbs on cue, then the turn and tell. Listen for a body clue plus a feeling.
